execution_scope: Source inspection plus temporary local fixture reproductions; the final event-ID substitution regression ran independently with 2 passes and 25 deselected. No services were started by the boundary review; service deployment acceptance is recorded separately.

findings.observed: A locally authenticated stored command naming an invented grant ID committed one fixture mutation; historical export/consume accepted that misattributed grant while still returning authorizes_execution=false.
findings.reproduction_boundary: Temporary explicit Runtime fixture; reviewer re-signed the command with its existing trusted fixture authority key and updated the stored command. This models a trusted producer semantic error, not an unauthenticated external exploit.
findings.resolution: Boundary fields now originate from actual returned authority/grant and must exactly match the signed command before check records or mutation.

findings.observed: Requiring the new checks input under the unchanged draft wire version would reject older serialized attempt bundles.
findings.resolution: Missing check proofs are accepted only after authenticating a legacy command with no execution-check marker; marked commands cannot downgrade.

findings.observed: Equality against version 1 accepted boolean True and floating 1.0.
findings.resolution: Explicit integer type and supported-version checks precede mutation and consumption.

findings.observed: Parent review found that a different authenticated lifecycle check event with the same attempt label could replace the actual event referenced by the attempt proof.
findings.resolution: The consumer now requires every exact authenticated check-proof event ID to appear among the lifecycle records, in addition to type, correlation and cardinality checks.

findings.observed: Independent review reproduced the analogous gap for COMMITTED evidence: keep the original commit proof, replace only its lifecycle row with a different authenticated COMMITTED event for the same attempt, and the prior consumer accepted it.
findings.reproduction_boundary: Temporary local fixture with an additional event signed by the trusted fixture writer; a trusted-producer semantic attribution issue, not unauthenticated authority or execution.
findings.resolution: The exact-ID requirement now includes the original commit proof as well as both check proofs; the substituted commit row is rejected.

findings.observed: Identical-authority refreshes persisting in reverse order could regress the last-observed timestamp.
findings.resolution: A same-revision, same-digest observation with an older timestamp retains the newer prior record. Real readonly-write and signed replay-trigger regression cases also cover preserving/authenticating stored observations.
findings.limits: The observation is diagnostic history only and never grants offline permission.

findings.observed: The adapter keys grants by skill and cannot preserve two resource scopes under one skill during a fresh recomputation. Existing coverage proves stale rejection only.
findings.resolution: Deferred coordinated plan in docs/MULTI_RESOURCE_GRANTS.md; no partial hidden projection implemented.

checked: Future interval ALLOW is insufficient for immediate grant; the trusted local clock must be within the interval.
The interval is signed into the scope binding; absolute expiry is capped at its exclusive end.
Grant-operation preflight and execution recheck the window after the synchronous policy call.
Operation replay preserves exact request/window identity and cannot turn a historical receipt into current permission.
Canonical policy supplies the evaluation timestamp and exact request/digest echoes; caller-supplied time is not authority.
recommended_regressions: PREPARED operation recovered after window end cancels without issue.
DISPATCHED unresolved operation after window end stays pending without blind redispatch.
Historical signed receipt recovered after window end finalizes evidence but cannot execute.
Execution policy call crossing the exclusive end prevents mutation.
limits: The fixed 2100-01-01 first-minute UTC interval is an explicitly configured demo rule, not a supplied business maintenance calendar.
Window enforcement trusts the local SystemClock; no cross-host clock-synchronization guarantee.
This review does not prove atomic distributed policy/authority mutation.

owner_regression_update.scope: UNIT service seams; source assertions independently inspected. Canonical normal/race and OPA evidence is maintained by the Foundation owner.

acceptance_reason: Review fixes are implemented and inspected; BDD031 remains open and this report is not live-service or product-value acceptance.
